Effect-size magnitude zones

Source: R/geom-es-zones.R
geom_es_zones.Rd

Draws background bands for effect-size magnitude zones ("negligible", "small", "medium", ...), symmetric around the null, behind estimates and confidence intervals. The layer draws a reference background only: it does not look at, classify or test any estimate.

Usage

geom_es_zones(
  thresholds,
  sd = NULL,
  scale = "identity",
  null = 0,
  softness = 0.1,
  palette = "grey",
  alpha = 0.35,
  orientation = "x",
  expand = FALSE,
  labels = FALSE,
  label_size = 3,
  label_colour = "grey20",
  n_slices = 40,
  title = NULL,
  show.legend = NA,
  ...
)

Arguments

thresholds

An es_thresholds() object, typically from es_benchmarks(). Required.

sd

Standard deviation used to convert standardised thresholds to the raw scale of the axis (see to_plot_scale()).

scale

"identity" for additive zones (null +/- cut), "log" for multiplicative zones around null (ratios on a log axis).

null

Position of the null on the axis: 0 for differences, 1 for ratios.

softness

Width of each soft transition as a fraction of the threshold it surrounds (on the log scale for multiplicative zones). 0 gives hard edges.

palette

"grey" (default, print-safe), "blue" (single hue), or a vector of colours: one per zone (lightest first) or two to interpolate between.

alpha

Opacity of the fills.

orientation

The axis that shows the effect: "x" (default, as in forest plots) or "y".

expand

If TRUE, all zone boundaries train the position scale.

labels

If TRUE, zone names are printed inside the panel, near the top (effect on the horizontal axis) or the right edge (vertical axis).

label_size, label_colour

Size (mm) and colour of zone labels.

n_slices

Number of thin rectangles used to draw each soft transition.

title

Legend title. Defaults to the short source of the thresholds.

show.legend

Should the zone legend be shown?

...

Other arguments passed to ggplot2::layer().

Value

An object that can be added to a ggplot with +.

Details

Add the layer before points, error bars and reference lines so that they are drawn on top of the zones.

Choosing thresholds

There is no default benchmark set; thresholds must be supplied. Cohen (1988) described his d = 0.2/0.5/0.8 as a fallback for when no better basis exists. Prefer thresholds grounded in your field (see es_benchmarks() for published sets, or build your own with es_thresholds()).

Scales and axes

The thresholds are converted with to_plot_scale() to the axis on which the estimates are drawn:

  • Standardised ("d") thresholds over raw mean differences: supply sd (e.g. pooled_sd() of the model). Which SD is appropriate is a substantive decision.

  • Odds or risk ratios: use scale = "log" with null = 1 and a log axis such as ggplot2::scale_x_log10(). With "d" thresholds and scale = "log", cut-points are converted to odds ratios by the Chinn (2000) approximation.

Zone positions are layer parameters, not data: with expand = FALSE (the default) they do not change the axis limits, and the outermost zones extend to the panel edges. With expand = TRUE every boundary is added to the scale range so all cut-points are visible.

Appearance

Fills are low-saturation and semi-transparent (alpha). The sequential ramp is lightest at the null and darkest in the largest zone, mirrored on both sides: direction carries no meaning in this mode. Boundaries are drawn as gradual transitions spanning softness times each threshold (softness = 0 gives hard edges), as a reminder that the cut-points are conventions, not natural discontinuities.

References

Cohen J (1988). Statistical Power Analysis for the Behavioral Sciences, 2nd ed. Hillsdale, NJ: Lawrence Erlbaum.

Chinn S (2000). A simple method for converting an odds ratio to effect size for use in meta-analysis. Statistics in Medicine 19(22):3127-3131.

See also

geom_mcid_zones(), plot_contrasts()

Examples

library(ggplot2)
fit <- aov(weight ~ group, data = PlantGrowth)
tk <- TukeyHSD(fit)$group
df <- data.frame(term = rownames(tk), estimate = tk[, "diff"],
                 lower = tk[, "lwr"], upper = tk[, "upr"])

ggplot(df, aes(estimate, term)) +
  geom_es_zones(es_benchmarks("cohen_d"), sd = pooled_sd(fit)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = 2) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = lower, xmax = upper), width = 0.2) +
  geom_point() +
  theme_minimal()


# Odds ratios on a log axis
or <- data.frame(term = c("A", "B", "C"), estimate = c(0.8, 1.9, 3.2),
                 lower = c(0.5, 1.2, 1.6), upper = c(1.3, 3.0, 6.4))
ggplot(or, aes(estimate, term)) +
  geom_es_zones(es_benchmarks("chen_or"), scale = "log", null = 1) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = lower, xmax = upper), width = 0.2) +
  geom_point() +
  scale_x_log10()
